title: improv·artist · cosmic (Refik Anadol)
mutation_directive: improv artist: cosmic via Refik Anadol

improv_extras.practice: data sculptures; AI-driven flow fields, memory of buildings, cosmic dust

v1.feedback: The Lucy silhouette is recognizable and well-framed, and the Anadol-inspired flow field with cosmic dust shedding genuinely reflects the brief — particles lifting off the surface in streams is a good translation of his data-sculpture language. The indigo-cyan-white palette is restrained and appropriate. To push further: the flow displacement is uniform enough that the surface reads as jittery rather than showing distinct current streams — try curl noise with fewer, stronger laminar bands so you get visible rivers of particles peeling away. The assembly animation from cosmic scatter is a nice touch but the breathing pulse adds visual noise without reinforcing the concept; replace it with a slow rotational drift so viewers can read the full 3D form without needing interaction.

v2.feedback: The Anadol flow-field-over-recognizable-form concept lands — Lucy silhouette reads instantly, palette is restrained and cosmic, band-based peeling is the right instinct. But the curl noise partial derivatives are botched (dny_dz, dnz_dy, dnx_dz etc. sample the wrong axes), so the streams will look more like random jitter than the laminar data-rivers that define Anadol's signature. Fix the curl math so streams visibly cohere along surface bands, and consider a less default mesh than Lucy — a building or cathedral scan would hit 'memory of buildings' harder and dodge the user's point-cloud-head-scan fatigue.
